translations.text: but we did not touch on the exposition any further than belonged to the honour of that day. Now we will run over the same gospel narrative again and give an exposition concerning this present feast.

It was fitting that a rational angel should make him known to the rational Jews, who knew God's law, and that to the heathens, who did not know divine reason, he should be revealed not through a voice but through a sign.
Concerning this Paul the apostle said, "The Saviour at his coming preached peace to us who were far off, and peace to those who were near."
The Jews who believed in Christ were nearer to him in place, and also through their knowledge of the old law;
Then they understood that the strange star signified the birth of the true King in the land over which it glided;
The astrologers went and worshipped, and the Jewish scribes, who had pointed out the place of birth through learning from books, stayed behind.
All creatures recognized the coming of their Creator, except the impious Jews alone.
The earth recognized him when it all trembled at his resurrection. Hell recognized him when it let its captives go against its will.
And yet the hard-hearted Jews would not, for all these signs, acknowledge the true Creator, whom the dumb creatures understood and made manifest by signs.
It did not glide before them the whole way, but after they came to the land of the Jews, it was then their guide, until it stood still above Christ's lodging.
Again we ask that no believing person defile his faith with this error.
Truly, holy scripture says that God loved Jacob and hated Esau; not because of fate, but because of their different deserts.
His deep righteousness would not force them to either, but gave them their own choice; for it is righteousness that each person be allowed his own choice.
Truly, those who now forsake God through their own choice and the devil's instigation, God also forsakes to eternal perdition.
Hold this firmly in your hearts: that the Almighty and Righteous God compels no one to sin, but he knows beforehand nonetheless which people will sin of their own will.
and he hates all those who work unrighteousness, and destroys those who speak lies. Truly, those who believe in God are guided by the Holy Spirit.
Let us offer him incense, in that we believe that he who at that time appeared as man was ever God.
Truly, the dead flesh rots sinfully when the mortal body serves flowing lust, as the prophet said about certain people, "The beasts rotted in their dung."
But if we offer the myrrh to God spiritually, then our mortal body will be kept from the stenches of lust through abstinence.
The first-created man and all his offspring were driven out of the joy of paradise through disobedience, and for eating the forbidden food,
and through pride, when he wished to be better than the Almighty Creator had made him.
